correctness.rationale: On dividing by q^n the recurrence reduces to u_(n+2)+u_(n+1)+u_n=0, giving the nonzero period-three weights −(t+1),1,t in residues 0,1,2. In a width-c column coefficient B_(C_c)(m+k,k), the normalization of the column cancels and shifting the ck factors by m gives q^(ckm). At each prime p the remaining contribution is ν_p(t)E_2+ν_p(t+1)E_0. Complete blocks of three in either sum contribute zero to each difference. Recounting the four nontrivial rectangle shapes, the pairs (E_0,E_2) at shifts 1,2 are: for 1×1, (0,1),(1,0); for 1×2 and 2×1, (1,0),(1,−1); for 2×2, (1,−1),(0,−1). Thus E_0≥0 and the only negative E_2 is −1 and requires ckm≥4. The case m=0 or k=0 gives one. This proves sufficiency at every width for t|q⁴, including each column entry (k=1). The witness B_f(4,2)=−q⁴(t+1)/t proves necessity by coprimality. Index divisibility forces t|q² via indices 2,4; conversely the only weight needing cancellation is t in a denominator at index i≡2 mod 3, and a proper multiple j supplies q^(j−i) with j−i≥2. For (q,t)=(2,8), f_2=32 and f_4=16 prove nondivisibility. Shapiro's Definition 4 and Corollary 10 confirm the all-level definition; §4.4 allows this recurrence (P=−q,Q=q²), and the integer sequences in Definition 1 may be signed. Frozen artifacts/check.py and its output were inspected, not run; arbitrary widths are handled by the exact residue argument.

value.rationale: Sharp all-level integrality across arbitrary column widths gives a concrete negative answer to the divisibility implication in a published question for signed nonzero integer sequences. The threshold is complete on this family and distinguishes all-level integrality from divisibility without claiming a positive-term counterexample or a general order-two classification.
